transcript:
Header: 2026-04-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia, Marcus, Kira — HealthSync: Janelle, Priya, Tom, Aaron

Summary (auto): quick walk through of this week's benchmark numbers, highlight where Redwood outperforms baseline and where we still need to tune, agree next steps for canary and deeper infra tests.

00:00 Sofia (AE): all right thanks everyone for joining, uh quick check — is this time still good? we have 45 minutes, we want to go over the benchmarks from yesterday's runs against MegaCloud, show some traces, and then sync on next steps
00:12 Janelle (CTO): yep this works, thanks. excited to see numbers — we had a noisy weekend on the baseline tests so curious how things look
00:20 Marcus (SE): cool, i'll share my screen — first slide is p50/p95/p99 for the 3 models you asked to test, 1) redwood-hosted quantized, 2) redwood-hosted with prefix cache, and 3) baseline provider default.
00:35 Marcus: the headline — p99 latency for Redwood quantized @ 384 prompt length is ~120ms, baseline p99 is ~220ms, so about 45% improvement on the tail — p50 is 28ms vs 45ms on baseline
00:52 Priya (ML Eng): are those warm-latency numbers? did you warm the kv cache?
00:58 Marcus: good question — this set is mixed: we ran cold start then a warm window; the prefix/KV cache run was a separate experiment showing p99 down to ~95ms once cache hits stabilize
01:12 Tom (SRE): what's throughput look like? tokens per second or requests per second? our workload is 1-3k concurrent users so throughput matters
01:20 Marcus: tokens/sec sustained — Redwood sustained about 1.8k tokens/sec when batching at 64 for the large model under our target sequence distribution, baseline sustained ~1.2k under similar batching. requests/sec numbers are in the sheet
01:34 Aaron (PM): that 1.8k number is for hosted right? how does dedicated look? any differences with autoscale config?
01:42 Marcus: dedicated runs were similar for single-zone tests but we didn't fully exercise autoscale yet. with dedicated and larger batch sizes we saw throughput up to 2.3k tokens/sec but p99 crept up slightly because of queuing — it's a latency vs cost tradeoff
01:59 Janelle: can you explain the quantization settings? we worry about quality regressions
02:04 Marcus: sure — we used int8 quant with per-channel calibration for the weights, and limited quant on attention kernels; we ran prompt-level evals against your holdout and didn't see significant regression in the rouge/bert-scores — i put the evals in the sheet but we should run a larger set
02:24 Priya: that matches what we need, still want to see a few edge-case prompts — i'll share a 10k set
02:31 Marcus: great, thanks. for quality sensitive paths you can pin to the float model; we also offer mixed quant profiles so you can route critical requests to the higher-fidelity variant
02:44 Kira (CSM): quick note on cost — our cost model shows quant + batching saves ~32% on token compute vs baseline for this workload; numbers in the cost tab of the spreadsheet
02:58 Janelle: interesting. what about tail spikes — MegaCloud had big spikes during our peak hour last week
03:06 Marcus: we looked at trace windows — the baseline's tail was correlated with autoscaling cold starts and queue buildup. in our runs, Redwood's continuous batching + cache warmed reduced cold start impact; traces show fewer 500ms+ events but there are still outliers when model eviction happens
03:28 Tom: eviction — is that GPU memory eviction? what's the eviction policy? we need to avoid noisy neighbor issues in shared hosted
03:37 Marcus: eviction here was the model sharder cleaning inactive key caches; on dedicated you'll have reserved pools and eviction is less likely. also we can adjust residency and kernel allocation to avoid frequent swaps
03:52 Aaron: any security concerns for hosted? we need SOC2 level logs and KMS integration
03:58 Sofia: yes we can provide SOC 2 docs and the KMS integration notes — i'll attach the security pack. we also support VPC private deployments if you want to test on-prem like network isolation
04:12 Janelle: okay good. about the canary — what are the criteria we should use to consider a canary successful vs baseline?
04:20 Marcus: suggested criteria: p99 within 1.5x baseline or strictly better, error rate <0.1% increase vs baseline, and quality metric (perplexity or task metric) within 2% of baseline. we can tweak those together
04:35 Priya: that sounds reasonable. also need to validate on your private deployment because our compliance folks want encryption at rest in our VPC
04:42 Sofia: yes we'll run a private pass; Marcus will help with infra and Tom will provision the VPC access.
04:50 Marcus: one more note on batching — we tuned adaptive batching so short sequences don't wait too long; the batching latency budget was set to 12ms which kept p50 low while increasing batching efficacy for longer sequences
05:05 Priya: you said batching at 64 earlier — is adaptive batching always using max batch=64?
05:11 Marcus: max batch 64 for those runs; adaptive tries to fill but not exceed the latency budget. for latency-sensitive routes we can set max batch lower or use cache-first routing
05:23 Janelle: what's the plan to run a comparable private benchmark? timeline?
05:28 Sofia: plan is to run a 24-hour soak in your test VPC next week after Tom provisions access. we'll run the same load generator and use your 10k prompt set. Marcus will run the scripts and then share traces and the runbook
05:40 Tom: i'll try to get the VPC ready by Thu 4/29, that's tight but doable
05:47 Marcus: perfect, we'll target the soak for Fri 4/30 and share results by Monday 5/4
05:54 Aaron: any other blockers? pricing? we still need the enterprise pricing for dedicated pools if we move forward
06:01 Sofia: i'll follow up with pricing; I'll include reserved commit options and a short TCO comparison based on your projected qps
06:10 Janelle: ok — wrap up please?
06:14 Sofia: Recap — we saw p99 improvement from ~220ms baseline to ~120ms with quantized Redwood hosted, throughput advantage ~1.8k vs 1.2k tokens/sec, next steps: Sofia send spreadsheet and raw traces by 4/23, Marcus deep dive week of 4/27, Priya share 10k prompts by 4/26, Tom provision VPC by 4/29, run 24h soak 4/30, results 5/4. we'll also attach SOC2 and KMS docs. thanks everyone
06:40 Janelle: thanks all
06:42 Meeting end

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (MegaCloud sometimes shown as 'mega cloud' in logs), speaker overlaps, and filler words. Links referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), runbook (link to internal gist), SOC2 pack (secure link).
